mainTopic: Covering blood on יום טוב: why a כוי's blood is not covered, mixed blood, and blood left from ערב יום טוב
overview: This amud asks why the blood of a כוי, an animal whose status is doubtful, may not be covered on יום טוב. The גמרא first shows that the person does have covering material, so the problem must be something else. רבה says אפר כירה is מוכן for a definite (ודאי) case but not for a doubtful (ספק) one. The גמרא tests two reasons for this. Making a hole (גומא) fails because of רבי אבא. Crushing (כתישה) also fails, because יום טוב is both an עשה and a לא תעשה, and an עשה alone cannot override both. רבא then explains that when the owner prepared the ashes, he only had definite needs in mind, which matches his ruling about earth brought in for צואה and דם צפור. רמי בריה דרב ייבא gives a different reason: a גזירה, so that people will not think the כוי is a חיה and eat its חלב. The amud ends with mixed blood, which may be covered only with one shovel thrust, and רבה's ruling that blood of a bird slaughtered on ערב יום טוב is not covered on יום טוב.

steps.title: The second half of the ruling shows he does have covering material
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא attacks the earlier explanation of why a כוי may not be slaughtered on יום טוב. The סיפא says 'if he slaughtered it, he does not cover its blood.' That only makes sense if he has something to cover with.
steps.simpleTranslation: But look, the later part of the teaching says: 'And if he did slaughter it, we do not cover its blood.' From this we learn that the first part is talking about someone who does have material to cover with!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is challenging the earlier answer, which said the case is one where the person has nothing prepared to cover the blood with.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If he had nothing to cover with, there would be no reason to say 'we don't cover its blood.' Obviously he couldn't. So the סיפא must be about someone who has prepared earth or אפר כירה. That forces the question: if he has it, why can't he use it for the כוי?

keyTerms.meaning: the later clause of a teaching
the first clause of a teaching
by implication; we can infer
the מצוה to cover the blood of a slaughtered wild animal or bird
where he has (material to cover with)

steps.confusionAlert: The phrase 'אין מכסין את דמו' does not mean he lacks material. The גמרא's whole point is the opposite: he has material, and still may not cover.

phrases.english: But from the fact that the latter clause teaches:

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם שְׁחָטוֹ — אֵין מְכַסִּין אֶת דָּמוֹ,
phrases.english: 'And if he slaughtered it, we do not cover its blood,'
it follows that (in the first clause) we are dealing with one who has [covering material]!
phrases.notes: The words in round brackets are in the standard printed גמרא, but some versions leave them out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the earlier explanation, found on the previous amud, that the case involves someone with no prepared covering material.
steps.kashyaTarget: The earlier answer that the case is one where he has nothing prepared to cover with
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The סיפא would be pointless unless he has material. So the case must involve someone who has material, and the earlier answer fails.

steps.title: רבה: stove ashes are prepared only for a definite case
steps.stepSummary: רבה gives a new answer. אפר כירה is considered prepared for covering blood in a ודאי case, but not in a ספק case like a כוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבה said: stove ashes are 'prepared' for a definite case, but are not 'prepared' for a doubtful case.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the old answer and brings רבה's new explanation of why the כוי's blood cannot be covered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ashes really are on hand, and the person meant to use them. But their 'prepared' status only covers a definite obligation. Since a כוי's blood is only possibly required to be covered, the ashes don't count as prepared for it.

keyTerms.meaning: ashes of a stove
prepared; allowed to be used on יום טוב
a definite case
a doubtful case

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the rest of this passage. Everything that follows is the search for why ודאי and ספק should be different.

phrases.english: Rather, Rabba said:
stove ashes are prepared for a definite case
and are not prepared for a doubtful case.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the answer that step 1 knocked down.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought the problem was that he had no material at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: He has material, but it only counts as מוכן for a definite obligation.

steps.title: Why not for a doubtful case? Maybe because of making a hole
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind רבה's distinction. It suggests a first possibility: taking ashes leaves a hole (גומא) in the pile.
steps.simpleTranslation: In a doubtful case, why not? Because he is making a hole [in the ash pile]?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the reason is behind רבה's rule and floats a first suggestion. This sets up the next challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Scooping ashes out of a pile leaves a pit, and digging a pit looks like a forbidden מלאכה. The idea is that we should not allow this for a mere ספק.

keyTerms.meaning: what is the reason?
a hole or pit
he makes or does

phrases.english: For a doubtful case, what is the reason not?
Because he makes a hole?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind רבה's rule.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the reason that ashes are not מוכן for a ספק?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Suggested: because he makes a גומא (hole).

steps.title: But a definite case also makes a hole
steps.stepSummary: The hole reason fails. Taking ashes in a ודאי case makes the same hole, yet that is allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: But in a definite case he also makes a hole!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the hole suggestion. If the hole were a problem, it would be a problem in a definite case too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A reason meant to explain why ודאי and ספק differ must apply only to the ספק. Making a hole happens in both cases, so it cannot explain the difference.

keyTerms.meaning: also

phrases.english: In a definite case he also makes a hole!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reason suggested in step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reason of גומא for the ספק case
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same hole is made in the ודאי case, which is permitted. So the hole cannot be what forbids the ספק.

steps.title: רבי אבא's principle cancels the hole concern in both cases
steps.stepSummary: The ודאי case is allowed because of רבי אבא. But the same principle would also allow the ספק case, so the hole reason is thrown out.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, [you must say the definite case is allowed] like רבי אבא. If so, here too [in the doubtful case] it should be allowed, like רבי אבא!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the hole is not a problem in a definite case. Then it shows that the same explanation removes the problem in a doubtful case too, so the hole suggestion collapses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אבא teaches that digging a hole when you only want the earth, not the hole, is not the forbidden digging. That principle doesn't care whether the case is ודאי or ספק. So 'hole' cannot be the reason for רבה's distinction.

keyTerms.meaning: here
in accordance with

phrases.english: Rather, [it is permitted] in accordance with Rabbi Abba;
here too, [it should be permitted] in accordance with Rabbi Abba!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא כִּדְרַבִּי אַבָּא, הָכָא נָמֵי כִּדְרַבִּי אַבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes off the hole suggestion. The very answer that permits ודאי also permits ספק.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole גומא explanation for רבה's rule
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי אבא's principle applies the same way to ודאי and ספק, so it cannot create a difference between them.

steps.title: New reason: he might crush the ashes
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא offers a different reason. In a ספק case we worry he might come to do כתישה (crushing clumps).
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: in a doubtful case, what is the reason? Perhaps he will do crushing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new reason for רבה's rule: the fear that the person will crush clumps of earth or ash to make them usable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Crushing clumps into fine powder resembles the forbidden מלאכה of grinding. So the concern is a גזירה (protective decree) against that.

keyTerms.meaning: crushing (clumps into powder), similar to the מלאכה of grinding
perhaps; lest

phrases.english: Rather: in a doubtful case, what is the reason?
Perhaps he will do crushing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the failed גומא reason with a new one.
steps.terutzMaskana: The problem is a possible act of כתישה.

steps.title: Then decree against a definite case too
steps.stepSummary: The same worry seems to exist in a ודאי case. So why not forbid that as well?
steps.simpleTranslation: In a definite case, too, let us decree because of crushing!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the crushing reason the same way it challenged the hole reason: it seems to apply to the definite case as well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The risk of crushing is the same whether the case is ודאי or ספק. So the challenge asks why the decree should be limited to ספק.

keyTerms.meaning: let us decree (a protective rabbinic rule)

phrases.english: In a definite case, too, let us decree because of crushing!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reason given in step 6.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The risk of crushing exists equally in ודאי, which is permitted. So why should it forbid ספק?

steps.title: In a definite case the positive מצוה overrides the prohibition
steps.stepSummary: In a ודאי case, even if he crushes, the עשה of כיסוי הדם overrides the לא תעשה of יום טוב. In a ספק case there is no definite עשה to override anything.
steps.simpleTranslation: In a definite case, even when he does crush, the positive commandment comes and pushes aside the negative commandment.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge and explains why crushing is a worry only in a doubtful case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עשה דוחה לא תעשה: a definite positive מצוה can override a prohibition. With a כוי, the obligation to cover is only a ספק. A doubtful מצוה cannot override a real prohibition, so we must worry about crushing there.

keyTerms.meaning: a positive commandment overrides a negative commandment
comes
pushes aside; overrides

steps.whatToRemember: At this stage, the כתישה approach says: אפר כירה is מוכן for a definite case of כיסוי הדם but not for a ספק like a כוי, because of a fear of כתישה. In a ודאי case, the עשה of covering overrides that prohibition. Note that step 11 knocks this approach out, and רבא replaces it in step 12.
steps.whyThisMatters: This answer is tested in the next steps. Step 9 questions the timing of the עשה, and step 11 shows that a single עשה cannot override יום טוב, which leads רבא to a new approach in step 12.

phrases.english: In a definite case, when he does crushing,

phrases.aramaic: אָתֵי עֲשֵׂה וְדָחֵי אֶת לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה.
phrases.english: the positive commandment comes and overrides the negative commandment.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָתֵי עֲשֵׂה וְדָחֵי אֶת לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 7 by distinguishing ודאי (where an עשה overrides) from ספק. Steps 9–11 then challenge this answer.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction based on the power of a definite עשה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The crushing concern should apply to ודאי as well.
steps.terutzMaskana: In ודאי, the עשה overrides the prohibition. In ספק, it cannot.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Provisional answer only: the כוי's blood is not covered because of possible כתישה, which a definite עשה could override but a doubtful one could not. Step 11 rejects this approach.

steps.title: The מצוה must happen at the same moment the prohibition is broken
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges Step 8. In the classic cases of עשה דוחה לא תעשה, the עשה is done at the very moment the לאו is broken. Here, crushing comes first and covering comes later.
steps.simpleTranslation: Fine, we say that a positive מצוה overrides a prohibition, as with מילה on skin that has צרעת, or a linen garment with woolen ציצית. But there, at the very moment he breaks the prohibition, he is doing the מצוה. Here, at the moment he breaks the prohibition by crushing, he is not yet doing the מצוה of covering!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from Step 8, which said the עשה of כיסוי הדם overrides יום טוב. It argues that this rule only works when the מצוה and the sin happen in one single action.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In מילה בצרעת, cutting the foreskin both removes the צרעת (the sin) and fulfills מילה (the מצוה) in one cut. In סדין בציצית, wearing the garment is both the כלאים and the ציצית at once. Crushing earth is a separate act that comes before covering, so at the moment of crushing no מצוה is being done.

keyTerms.meaning: A positive מצוה overrides a prohibition
Circumcision on skin that has צרעת, even though cutting off צרעת is normally forbidden
A linen garment with woolen ציצית, even though wool and linen together is כלאים
At the moment / at the same time
Uprooting (breaking) a prohibition

steps.confusionAlert: This is NOT asking whether עשה דוחה לא תעשה is a real rule. It is. The question is only whether it applies when the מצוה and the sin happen at two different moments.

phrases.english: Say that we do say

phrases.aramaic: אָתֵי עֲשֵׂה וְדָחֵי אֶת לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה
phrases.english: a positive מצוה comes and overrides a prohibition
such as circumcision on skin with tzara'as,
or also a linen garment with tzitzis.
For at the moment that he uproots the prohibition,
he is fulfilling the positive מצוה.
Here, at the moment that he uproots the prohibition,
phrases.notes: The prohibition here is crushing the clumps of earth (כתישה).

phrases.english: he is not fulfilling the positive מצוה!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימַר דְּאָמְרִינַן אָתֵי עֲשֵׂה וְדָחֵי אֶת לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the mechanism used in Step 8
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in Step 8 that the עשה of כיסוי הדם overrides the לאו of יום טוב in a ודאי case
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: עשה דוחה לא תעשה requires the מצוה and the transgression to happen at the same moment. Crushing comes before covering, so the rule should not apply.

steps.title: He covers while he crushes
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the crushing and covering can happen together. He crushes the clumps directly onto the blood, so the covering happens at the same moment.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is not difficult, because while he is crushing, he is covering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends Step 8. It says the person crushes the earth right over the blood, so crushing and covering happen as one act.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumed crushing and covering are two separate steps. The answer removes that assumption: the crushed earth falls onto the blood as it is crushed. Now the sin and the מצוה happen at the same moment, just like מילה בצרעת.

keyTerms.meaning: This is not difficult
Crushes (clumps of earth)
Covers (the blood)

phrases.english: This is not difficult,
for at the same time that he crushes, he is covering.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא לָא קַשְׁיָא, דְּבַהֲדֵי דְּכָתֵישׁ קָא מִכַּסֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 9
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the case so the two actions happen together
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Crushing and covering are two separate moments, so the עשה cannot override the לאו
steps.terutzMaskana: Crushing happens right over the blood, so the מצוה is done at the same moment as the transgression

steps.title: יום טוב is both a positive and a negative command
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא raises a stronger problem. יום טוב has both an עשה and a לאו, and an עשה alone cannot override a לאו that comes with an עשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the end, יום טוב is both a positive מצוה and a prohibition, and a positive מצוה does not override a prohibition together with a positive מצוה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the whole idea of Step 8 from a new direction. Even if the timing works, the עשה of כיסוי הדם is not strong enough to override יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יום טוב has a positive command to rest (שבתון) and a prohibition against doing work. The rule is that one עשה cannot push aside a לאו plus an עשה. So the כיסוי הדם explanation collapses completely, even for a ודאי case.

keyTerms.meaning: In the end / ultimately. It signals a challenge that remains even after the last answer
A positive command together with a prohibition
A positive command does not override

steps.whyThisMatters: This challenge is strong enough to knock out the כיסוי הדם approach entirely. That is why the next step opens with אלא and starts fresh.

phrases.english: In the end,

phrases.aramaic: יוֹם טוֹב עֲשֵׂה וְלֹא תַעֲשֶׂה הוּא —
phrases.english: Yom Tov is a positive command and a prohibition,
and a positive command does not override
a prohibition together with a positive command!

steps.triggerLanguage: סוֹף סוֹף, יוֹם טוֹב עֲשֵׂה וְלֹא תַעֲשֶׂה הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Renews the attack on Step 8 after Step 10's defense
steps.kashyaTarget: The use of עשה דוחה לא תעשה to allow crushing in a ודאי case
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: יום טוב carries both an עשה and a לאו, and a single עשה cannot override that combination

steps.title: רבא: The ashes were set aside only for definite cases
steps.stepSummary: רבא drops the earlier approach and gives a new reason. When the stove ashes were prepared before יום טוב, the owner intended them only for definite cases. He did not intend them for doubtful ones.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: For stove ashes, his intention is for a definite case, and his intention is not for a doubtful case.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא throws out the כתישה approach and brings רבא's new answer. The difference between ודאי and ספק depends on what the owner had in mind for the ashes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On יום טוב you may only use items that were prepared (מוכן) before the holiday for that use. A person setting aside stove ashes thinks of covering blood that he definitely must cover, not blood of a doubtful כוי. So for a ספק case the ashes count as unprepared and may not be used.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather. It rejects the previous approach and introduces a new one
Ashes of a stove, which were prepared before יום טוב
His intention / what he had in mind
Prepared beforehand for use on יום טוב (the opposite of מוקצה)

steps.whatToRemember: The final reason why a ספק may not be covered on יום טוב is not about crushing or holes. The ashes were prepared only for definite cases, so using them for a doubtful case is like using something not prepared for יום טוב.
steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not saying the ספק blood should not be covered at all. He is only saying that these ashes were never set aside for that use on יום טוב.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shifts the whole question from the laws of work on יום טוב to the laws of מוכן and מוקצה, meaning what was intended before the holiday.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
stove ashes, his intention is for a definite case,
and his intention is not for a doubtful case.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the כתישה approach (Steps 6-10) after Step 11 destroyed it
steps.terutzResolutionType: New reason replacing the failed one
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ספק is forbidden because of a worry about crushing, and the ודאי is allowed because of עשה דוחה לא תעשה
steps.terutzMaskana: The ashes were prepared only for definite cases, so they may not be used for a ספק
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The owner's intention when preparing stove ashes covers ודאי cases only, which explains why a ספק may not be covered on יום טוב

steps.title: רבא is consistent with his ruling about earth for excrement
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that רבא's idea in Step 12, that a person prepares only for definite uses, matches another ruling of his. Earth brought in to cover צואה may be used for דם צפור, but earth brought in for דם צפור may not be used for צואה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא follows his own reasoning, because רבא said: if someone brought in earth to cover excrement, he may use it to cover a bird's blood. If he brought it in for a bird's blood, he may not use it to cover excrement.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that רבא's answer in Step 12 is not new for him. He holds the same idea in a different case about covering excrement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Covering a baby's צואה is a doubtful need, since the baby may not dirty the house. Someone who prepares earth even for that doubtful need surely also has in mind the definite need of covering דם צפור, so both uses are allowed. Someone who prepares earth for the definite need of דם צפור never thought about the doubtful need, so that earth stays מוקצה for צואה.

keyTerms.meaning: He follows his own reasoning, meaning he is consistent with another ruling of his
He brought in earth before יום טוב, setting it aside for use
Excrement, here a baby's mess that may or may not happen
The blood of a slaughtered bird, which must be covered (כיסוי הדם)

steps.confusionAlert: This can feel backwards. The earth prepared for the doubtful use (צואה) is the one with wider permission. Whoever plans for something that may not happen certainly also plans for something that definitely will happen.

phrases.english: And Rava follows his own reasoning,
for Rava said:
If he brought in earth to cover excrement with it,
phrases.notes: Covering excrement is something he only might end up needing.

phrases.english: it is permitted to cover a bird's blood with it.
phrases.notes: Covering the blood is something he definitely needs, so it counts as part of what he brought the earth for.

phrases.english: If he brought it for a bird's blood,
it is forbidden to cover excrement with it.
phrases.notes: The uncertain need was not in his mind.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports Step 12 by showing that רבא holds the same principle elsewhere.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Earth prepared for a doubtful use may serve a definite use, but earth prepared for a definite use may not serve a doubtful use.

steps.title: The נהרבלאי allow both directions
steps.stepSummary: The נהרבלאי disagree with רבא. Even earth brought in for דם צפור may be used to cover צואה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages of נהרבלא say: even if he brought in earth to cover a bird's blood, he may use it to cover excrement.
steps.whatsHappening: A different group of rabbis argues with רבא's ruling from Step 13.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The נהרבלאי do not accept the idea that a person's preparation covers only definite uses. In their view, once the earth was prepared, it may be used for doubtful needs such as צואה as well.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages of נהרבלא, a town in Babylonia
Even, introducing a more lenient ruling

phrases.english: The Sages of Neharbela say:

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ הִכְנִיס עָפָר לְכַסּוֹת בּוֹ דַּם צִפּוֹר —
phrases.english: Even if he brought in earth to cover a bird's blood with it,
it is permitted to cover excrement with it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the second half of רבא's ruling in Step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Earth prepared for דם צפור may also be used to cover צואה.

steps.title: A dispute in ארץ ישראל about whether a כוי is like excrement
steps.stepSummary: In ארץ ישראל it was reported that two אמוראים disagree. There are two versions of who they were. One holds that a כוי is like צואה, meaning a doubtful case. The other holds that it is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the West they say: רבי יוסי בר חמא and רבי זירא disagree about this. Some say it was רבא son of רב יוסף בר חמא and רבי זירא. One said a כוי is like excrement, and one said a כוי is not like excrement.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports an argument about whether a כוי belongs in the same group as צואה. This sets up the next step, which identifies which side רבא was on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is whether earth brought in to cover צואה may also be used for a כוי's blood. One view says a כוי is like צואה: both are uncertain needs, so earth prepared for צואה may cover a כוי's blood too. The other view says covering צואה is common enough to count as a definite need compared with a כוי, so that earth may not be used for a כוי.

keyTerms.meaning: In the West, meaning ארץ ישראל
They disagree
An animal whose status (wild animal or domesticated animal) is doubtful, so covering its blood is only a doubtful obligation

phrases.english: They say in the West (Eretz Yisrael):

phrases.aramaic: פְּלִיגִי בַּהּ רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר חָמָא וְרַבִּי זֵירָא,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei bar Chama and Rabbi Zeira disagree about it,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרִי לַהּ רָבָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יוֹסֵף בַּר חָמָא וְרַבִּי זֵירָא.
phrases.english: and some say it was Rava son of Rav Yosef bar Chama and Rabbi Zeira.
phrases.notes: This is the same רבא known throughout the Bavli.

phrases.aramaic: חַד אָמַר: כּוֹי, הֲרֵי הוּא כְּצוֹאָה.
phrases.english: One said: a koy is like excrement.
And one said: a koy is not like excrement.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a related dispute about whether the doubtful-use principle applies to a כוי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two אמוראים dispute whether a כוי is treated like צואה. The next step identifies which side רבא holds.

steps.title: Proof that רבא said a כוי is like excrement
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proves that רבא is the one who said a כוי is like צואה. This matches his ruling that a person prepares only for definite needs, not doubtful ones.
steps.simpleTranslation: We can conclude that רבא is the one who said a כוי is like excrement, because רבא said: earth brought in for excrement may cover a bird's blood, but earth brought in for a bird's blood may not cover excrement. Conclude it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles which version of the dispute is correct by using רבא's known ruling from Step 13.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's ruling treats צואה as an uncertain need, and he says a person who prepares earth for an uncertain need also has other needs in mind. A כוי is also an uncertain case, so for רבא it is on the same level as צואה. That is the view 'a כוי is like צואה.' It also fits Step 12: ashes prepared with only definite needs in mind may not be used for the doubtful כוי.

keyTerms.meaning: Conclude it, meaning it is proven

steps.whatToRemember: רבא's principle is that what is prepared before יום טוב covers definite needs only, not doubtful ones. This is why the ashes may cover the blood of a definite חיה but not the blood of a כוי.
steps.whyThisMatters: This closes the section. It confirms that רבא's answer in Step 12 rests on a consistent principle about a person's intention when he prepares something for יום טוב.

phrases.english: Conclude that Rava is the one who said
a koy is like excrement,
for Rava said:
If he brought in earth to cover excrement with it,
it is permitted to cover a bird's blood with it;

phrases.aramaic: דַּם צִפּוֹר — אָסוּר לְכַסּוֹת בּוֹ צוֹאָה.
phrases.english: if for a bird's blood, it is forbidden to cover excrement with it.
Conclude it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the attribution question raised in Step 15.
steps.raayaObject: That רבא holds a כוי is like צואה
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבא's own ruling about earth prepared for צואה versus דם צפור
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבא is the one who holds that a כוי is like צואה, meaning a doubtful case not covered by earth prepared for definite needs.

steps.title: A new reason: covering the blood could lead people to permit the forbidden fat
steps.stepSummary: רמי בריה דרב ייבא says we do not cover a כוי's blood because of a rabbinic גזירה. People might conclude that a כוי is definitely a חיה and eat its חלב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי, the son of רב ייבא, said: The reason we do not cover the blood of a כוי is a rabbinic decree, because of the risk that its fat will be treated as permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: A new אמורא gives a completely different reason why we do not cover the blood of a כוי on יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the reason was about the earth: it was only prepared for definite cases, not doubtful ones. רמי בריה דרב ייבא says the real issue is what people will conclude from seeing it. כיסוי הדם is done only for a חיה or עוף, and the חלב of a חיה is permitted. So if people see the blood being covered, they may decide a כוי is a חיה and wrongly eat its חלב.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal whose status is in doubt: it may be a בהמה (domesticated animal) or a חיה (wild animal)
A protective decree made by the רבנן to keep people from making a mistake
Permitting its fat. The חלב of a בהמה is forbidden, but the חלב of a חיה is permitted
We cover (the blood)

steps.confusionAlert: This is NOT about the act of covering being forbidden work on יום טוב. The worry is only about the wrong message people might take from seeing the blood covered.

phrases.english: Rami, son of Rav Yeiva, said:
A koy: this is the reason that we do not cover (its blood)
It is a decree because of (people) permitting its fat.
phrases.notes: People might think a כוי is a חיה, whose חלב is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different reason from רבא's explanation (a person prepares earth only for definite needs) for why a כוי's blood is not covered.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: We do not cover a כוי's blood because of a גזירה: covering might lead people to permit its חלב.

steps.title: Then the same worry should apply on a weekday too
steps.stepSummary: If the worry is that people will permit the חלב, that worry exists on weekdays too. So why do we cover a כוי's blood on a weekday?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, then even on a weekday we should also not cover it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רמי בריה דרב ייבא: his reason does not seem to be limited to יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry about the חלב has nothing to do with the day of the week. Yet on a weekday a כוי's blood is covered (as the משנה in חולין teaches). So the reason seems to prove too much.

keyTerms.meaning: If so (if your reason is correct)
On a weekday (a regular, non-holy day)

phrases.english: If so, even on a weekday as well (we should not cover)!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reason given in Step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: רמי בריה דרב ייבא's reason (the גזירה about the חלב)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The worry about permitting the חלב applies on any day. Yet on a weekday the blood is covered, so the reason does not explain why only יום טוב is different.

steps.title: On a weekday people assume he is just cleaning his yard
steps.stepSummary: On a weekday, onlookers will think he is covering the blood only to keep his courtyard clean, not to do the מצוה of כיסוי הדם.
steps.simpleTranslation: On a weekday, people say: he needs to clean his courtyard.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by explaining why people would not misunderstand on a weekday.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On a weekday, covering the blood can be explained as simple tidying, so no one learns anything about the כוי's status from it. On יום טוב, people would not bother tidying in this way. So covering there looks like a מצוה, and that would suggest the כוי is a חיה.

keyTerms.meaning: To clean (tidy) his courtyard

phrases.english: On a weekday, (people) say
he needs (to do this) to clean his courtyard.

steps.triggerLanguage: בַּחוֹל אָמְרִי לְנַקֵּר חֲצֵרוֹ הוּא צָרִיךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing how onlookers read the action on a weekday versus on יום טוב
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The חלב worry should apply equally on a weekday.
steps.terutzMaskana: On a weekday, the covering is seen as cleaning, so no one draws a conclusion about the כוי's status.

steps.title: Two cases where the cleaning explanation does not work
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the 'cleaning' answer. If he slaughtered on a trash heap, no one would think he is cleaning. And if he came to ask a חכם whether to cover, the ruling itself sends a message.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he slaughtered on a garbage heap, what is there to say? If he came to ask (a Sage), what is there to say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pokes holes in the last answer with two cases where 'he is just cleaning' cannot be the explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A garbage heap does not need cleaning, so covering blood there clearly looks like the מצוה. A person who asks a רב and is told to cover will think the רב is treating the כוי as a חיה. In both cases the worry about the חלב comes back, even on a weekday.

keyTerms.meaning: A garbage or dung heap
He came to consult (to ask a חכם what to do)
What is there to say? (The answer does not work here)

phrases.english: (If) he slaughtered on a garbage heap,
what is there to say?
(If) he came to consult (a Sage),
what is there to say?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of Step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that on a weekday people assume he is cleaning his courtyard
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In some cases the 'cleaning' explanation is impossible (a garbage heap) or does not apply (a direct ruling from a חכם). There the חלב worry should still exist on a weekday.

steps.title: On weekdays the רבנן ask him to cover even a doubtful case, but not on יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: New answer: on a weekday the רבנן tell a person to make the effort and cover even a doubtful case, so covering proves nothing. On יום טוב they would never ask for that effort in a doubt, so covering would signal that the כוי is definitely a חיה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: on a weekday, even if it is a doubt, the Sages tell him: Go, make the effort and cover. On יום טוב, if it is a doubt, would the Sages tell him: Go, make the effort and cover?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the 'cleaning' answer and gives a better reason why the חלב worry applies only on יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone knows that on a weekday the רבנן tell people to cover blood even when it is only a ספק, so a covered כוי teaches nothing about its status. On יום טוב the רבנן do not ask people to go to that trouble for a mere doubt. So if a כוי's blood were covered on יום טוב, people would conclude it must be a definite חיה, and they would permit its חלב. That is why the גזירה applies only on יום טוב.

keyTerms.meaning: It is a doubt (an uncertain case)
Go, make the effort, and cover
The Sages (the חכמים)
On a Festival

steps.whatToRemember: According to רמי בריה דרב ייבא, we do not cover a כוי's blood on יום טוב only because of the message it would send. On a weekday, covering is expected even for a doubtful case, so it signals nothing. On יום טוב, covering would signal that the כוי is definitely a חיה, and people would then eat its חלב.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a key principle: the same action can send different messages on different days. A גזירה can depend on how the public will read an action in a specific setting.

phrases.english: Rather: on a weekday, even if it is a doubt,
the Sages say to him:
Go, make the effort, and cover.
On a Festival, if it is a doubt —
would the Sages say to him:
Go, make the effort, and cover?
phrases.notes: No. So covering on יום טוב would look like a ruling that the כוי is definitely a חיה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: בְּחוֹל [אִי נָמֵי] מִסְּפֵקָא, אָמְרִי לֵיהּ רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected answer of Step 19 and resolves both the original קשיא (Step 18) and the follow-up cases (Step 20).
steps.terutzResolutionType: Revised answer (אלא): distinguishing what the רבנן require for a doubt on a weekday versus on יום טוב
steps.terutzHavaAmina: On a weekday people would think he is only cleaning his courtyard.
steps.terutzMaskana: Weekday covering is required even for a doubt, so it sends no message. Covering on יום טוב would imply a definite חיה, so the רבנן forbade it.

steps.title: Mixed blood may not be covered on יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא teaches a ברייתא: the ban on covering is not only for a כוי. If the blood of a בהמה, a חיה, and an עוף got mixed, it is also forbidden to cover it on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא taught: The rule was not said only about a כוי. Even if someone slaughtered a בהמה, a חיה, and an עוף, and their blood got mixed together, it is forbidden to cover it on יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that adds a second case to the כוי rule: a mixture of blood that needs covering with blood that does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Blood of a חיה or עוף must be covered, but blood of a בהמה does not need covering. In a mixture, part of the covering work goes to the בהמה blood, which is extra work with no מצוה. Extra work like that is not allowed on יום טוב.

keyTerms.meaning: Domesticated animal (its blood does not need covering)
Wild animal and bird (their blood must be covered)
Became mixed

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think בהמה blood is forbidden to cover because of a doubt, like the כוי. Here nothing is in doubt. The problem is that some of the covering work is wasted on blood that has no מצוה.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira taught:
Not only about a koy did they say this,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אֲפִילּוּ שָׁחַט בְּהֵמָה, חַיָּה וָעוֹף
phrases.english: but even if one slaughtered a domesticated animal, a wild animal, and a bird
and their blood became mixed together
it is forbidden to cover it on Yom Tov.
phrases.notes: Covering includes work for the בהמה blood, which has no מצוה.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנֵי רַבִּי זֵירָא: לֹא כּוֹי בִּלְבַד אָמְרוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the כוי rule from Steps 17-21 to a new case of mixed blood.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A mixture of בהמה, חיה, and עוף blood may not be covered on יום טוב.

steps.title: Limitation: one shovel thrust is allowed
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי בר יאסיניאה says the ban on mixed blood applies only when covering takes more than one thrust. If one thrust covers it all, it is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי בר יאסיניאה said: They taught this only when he cannot cover it with one thrust of the shovel. But if he can cover it with one thrust, it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: An אמורא narrows the ברייתא's ban to cases that need more than one shovel thrust.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With one thrust, all the blood is covered in a single act, and that act is needed for the מצוה anyway. No extra work is added for the בהמה blood. With two thrusts, one thrust may be only for the בהמה blood, and that is the extra work the ברייתא forbids.

keyTerms.meaning: They only taught this in the case of (a limiting formula)
A thrust or stab of the shovel into the earth
Permitted

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the problem with mixed blood is extra work, not the act of covering itself.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei bar Yasinia said:
They taught this only
when he cannot cover it with one thrust,
but if he can cover it with one thrust
it is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא שֶׁאֵין יָכוֹל לְכַסּוֹתוֹ בִּדְקִירָה אַחַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the ברייתא of Step 22 to cases that need more than one thrust.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Mixed blood may be covered on יום טוב if one thrust covers it all.

steps.title: Isn't that obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי יוסי בר יאסיניאה needed to say this, since it seems obvious.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יוסי בר יאסיניאה: his ruling seems too obvious to need saying. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If one thrust covers everything, he is simply doing the מצוה and adds no extra work. So why would anyone think it is forbidden? The גמרא wants to know what new point the statement teaches.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious! (a challenge asking why a statement is needed)

phrases.english: It is obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks Step 23 as an unnecessary statement.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling of רבי יוסי בר יאסיניאה that one thrust is permitted.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One thrust adds no extra work, so the permission seems self-evident and not worth stating.

steps.title: We might have banned one thrust because of two
steps.stepSummary: The statement is needed. We might have thought the רבנן banned even one thrust so that people would not come to use two. He teaches that there is no such גזירה.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: let us make a גזירה against one thrust because of two thrusts. So he teaches us that we do not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by showing the possible mistake that the statement prevents.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without this statement, we might have thought the רבנן made a גזירה: ban even one thrust, because people might do two. רבי יוסי בר יאסיניאה teaches that the רבנן made no such גזירה, so one thrust stays permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said (introduces a mistaken assumption)
Let us make a rabbinic decree
Because of, out of concern for
He teaches us (this is the new point)

steps.whatToRemember: Mixed blood: two thrusts are forbidden on יום טוב because of the extra work. One thrust is permitted, and there is no גזירה against it.

phrases.english: You might have said:

phrases.aramaic: נִגְזַר דְּקִירָה אַחַת אַטּוּ שְׁתֵּי דְקִירוֹת,
phrases.english: let us decree against one thrust because of two thrusts,
so he teaches us that we do not.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא: נִגְזַר דְּקִירָה אַחַת אַטּוּ שְׁתֵּי דְקִירוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the פשיטא of Step 24.
steps.terutzResolutionType: מהו דתימא: the statement prevents a mistaken assumption that a גזירה exists.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The רבנן might have banned one thrust as a fence against two thrusts.
steps.terutzMaskana: There is no גזירה. One thrust is fully permitted.

steps.title: A bird slaughtered before יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: רבה rules that if someone slaughtered a bird on ערב יום טוב, its blood may not be covered on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: If someone slaughtered a bird on ערב יום טוב, we do not cover its blood on יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic with a ruling from רבה about blood left uncovered from before יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Covering blood on יום טוב is allowed only as part of a שחיטה done on יום טוב for food. Here the שחיטה happened the day before, and the covering could have been done then. So digging and covering now is not permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: A bird
The day before יום טוב
We do not cover

steps.confusionAlert: The blood still needs covering by Torah law. The ruling only says this covering may not be done on יום טוב itself.

phrases.english: Rabba said:
If one slaughtered a bird on the eve of Yom Tov,
we do not cover its blood on Yom Tov.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה: שָׁחַט צִפּוֹר מֵעֶרֶב יוֹם טוֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new case about covering blood on יום טוב, separate from the כוי and mixture discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Blood of a bird slaughtered on ערב יום טוב may not be covered on יום טוב.
